newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes ease late.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes ease late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes kept easing late, as West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell and buying faded on expectations that further discounts would appear as supplies backed-up amid refinery maintenance.

Trade faded early as players awaited monthly prorationing on Arco's Line 63, a major conduit into Los Angeles refineries. Limits were set at 46.06 percent of nominations in line with forecasts but slightly tighter than last month.
Fixed deltas for Line 63 crude, whose shipments are constrained because of limited line space remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under WTI with postings basis at $1.00.
Discounts for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude were flat at $2.30 a barrel under WTI. Talk was light with most buyers balanced for October and further weakness seen for November.
Meanwhile, cash WTI fell five cents from early levels to $23.40/23.50 a barrel with stocks ample and refiners bargain hunting for crude in preparation for autumn production cuts.
Prices for California Kern River crude remained $16.15/16.35 a barrel.
And prices for lightly traded Wilmington crude oil held at $17.60/17.70.
